The Example Highway Works Regulations 2020

Made 12 February 2020

3. Notice of works

(1) A person who intends to carry out works on a highway must give notice of the works to the authority for that highway. This is sample text written for a test. It is not the text of any real regulation, and it should not be read as law.

(2) The notice must say where the works will be, what they are for, and when they are expected to start and finish. It must be given in writing, and it may be given by email if the authority has said that it accepts notices by email.

(3) The authority may ask for more information if the notice does not give enough detail for it to decide whether the works will affect other users of the highway. A person who is asked for more information must provide it within a reasonable time.

(4) Where works are needed urgently to prevent danger, the person carrying them out may begin before giving notice, but must give notice as soon as reasonably practicable afterwards and must say why the works could not wait.

(5) A notice given under this regulation does not give a person any right to carry out works that they would not otherwise be entitled to carry out. It is only a record that the authority has been told about the works.

(6) The authority must keep a record of each notice it receives for at least as long as the works are in progress and for a further period afterwards. The record must be available for inspection by anyone with a proper interest in the works.

(7) In this regulation, “works” includes any work to a highway or to apparatus on or under it, whether or not the work is temporary. A reference to the authority is to the authority responsible for maintaining the highway concerned.

(8) Where more than one person is involved in carrying out works, a notice given by one of them is treated as given by all of them, provided that the notice names every person who is involved and says which of them is the main contact for the authority.
